scope: Round5 external physical validation; old round4 56/112 records are regression only

objects.suspicion_detection: An APAR rule-family violation is present for a sustained eligible window. This is a fault signal, not a unique component diagnosis.
objects.fault_detection: Binary any-fault comparison made after inference against the independent CSV ground-truth label; all normal and fault cases remain in the denominator.
objects.fault_localization: A component attribution is counted only when the declared component matches the independent experiment label. Unsupported damper attribution is an error, not a correct suspicion.
objects.next_action_correctness: Whether the requested point/time/action is independently judged appropriate. No participant or independent expert review exists yet, so this remains unscored.
objects.coverage: Resolved candidate state / all cases; unresolved and not-testable cases remain in the denominator.
objects.external_applicability: Cases with all required points, valid actual time intervals, and at least one eligible APAR window divided by all selected experiment days; this is a data applicability ratio, not diagnostic accuracy.

methods.apar: NISTIR6994 APAR rules adapted to the documented FLEXLAB SZVAV sequence; no workflow consistency gate.
methods.apar_plus_verification: The same APAR rules, input points, calibration, thresholds and windows, with the predeclared independent inlet-temperature consistency check before damper-related suspicion is reported.
methods.without_consistency: Necessary ablation: the same APAR-plus-verification path with only the inlet-temperature consistency check removed. It is not a weak baseline.

rules: No label, date, fault filename, injection setting or ground-truth field enters adapter signals or APAR evaluation.
All cases, dates, normal controls and fault controls are scored.
A no-alarm result never implies normal equipment.
Control command is not actual actuator feedback; damper attribution is conditional and may remain unresolved.
